items.headline: Woman, 30, dies in a collision at Queen Street Bus Terminal; bus driver, 32, arrested
items.summary: The woman was pronounced dead at the Bugis terminal on the evening of 6 October after being pinned under a bus; police arrested the 32-year-old driver for careless driving causing death.

items.headline: Man, 33, jailed two years and three months for secretly filming his wife and mother bathing
items.summary: He pleaded guilty to four of 10 charges after recording the women and sending the footage to others; the remaining charges were taken into consideration.

items.headline: Two men jailed and caned over a Geylang nightclub assault sparked by a staring dispute
items.summary: On 5 October one attacker was sentenced to 18 months and four strokes and Tan Swee Heng, 45, to one year five months and three strokes, over the April 2025 beating at a Geylang club.

items.headline: Hong Kong's monetary authority questions HSBC over siting its AI centre in Singapore
items.summary: The HKMA asked HSBC why its new Global AI Centre of Excellence will open in Singapore rather than Hong Kong, the bank's largest market, the Financial Times reported. HSBC declined to comment.

items.headline: Update: Rupee sinks toward a record low even after the RBI's rate hike
items.summary: A day after the RBI's first rate increase in nearly four years, the rupee fell as much as 0.4% to 96.85 per dollar, close to its all-time low of 96.965, as oil prices and global yields weighed.

items.headline: RBI signals more tightening as economists forecast back-to-back rate hikes
items.summary: Economists expect another quarter-point increase at the RBI's 4 December meeting, with some seeing the policy rate rising to 6.25% from 5.5% by the first half of 2027.

items.headline: India's Nifty 50 posts its longest weekly losing streak in 25 years
items.summary: The benchmark has fallen for eight straight weeks and slipped below its 200-week moving average as a weak monsoon and foreign outflows weigh on sentiment.

items.headline: Two Latvian nationals charged after breaking into an RAF base used by US forces
items.summary: Counterterrorism police said the pair were arrested in Cambridgeshire after entering a UK airbase used by American forces, adding to scrutiny of security around US assets in Britain.

items.headline: Greens' Zack Polanski takes on Labour in the Holborn & St Pancras by-election
items.summary: Voters chose a successor for Keir Starmer's old north London seat on 8 October, with Green leader Zack Polanski challenging Labour's Sagal Abdi-Wali; bookmakers favoured Labour to hold.

items.headline: Reform UK stumbles as PM Burnham's Labour regains momentum in the polls
items.summary: After Andy Burnham won the Makerfield by-election in June, Labour has extended its polling lead while Nigel Farage's Reform UK grapples with a campaign-finance investigation.

items.headline: Russian strike kills at least 33 in eastern Ukraine in one of the year's deadliest attacks
items.summary: CNN reported a Russian strike in the east killed at least 33 people amid an intensifying pre-winter barrage; Ukraine's grid operator ordered emergency outages in Kyiv.

items.headline: India, Turkiye, Egypt and the US float new proposals for a Russia-Ukraine truce
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that several governments have put forward ceasefire proposals aimed at protecting global energy supplies and shipping, as diplomats test the prospects for a pause.

items.headline: Israel sets a deadline to shut the UK consulate in East Jerusalem over settler sanctions
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported Israel ordered the closure of the office handling Britain's ties with Palestinians, in retaliation for UK sanctions on settlers, with last-minute talks seeking to avert a full shutdown.

items.headline: Israeli attacks across Gaza kill at least four Palestinians, including a rescue worker
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported Israeli strikes killed at least four people and wounded others across Gaza, including a rescue worker near Kamal Adwan Hospital, as marches marking three years since 7 October were held worldwide.

items.headline: Healthleap raises $38 million for AI that flags hospital patients needing a closer look
items.summary: The platform reads patient records to surface people who may have undiagnosed illnesses. It closed an $8 million seed co-led by Sequoia and First Round and a $30 million Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures.

items.headline: Nous Research raises a reported $90 million and launches an enterprise AI-agent platform
items.summary: The startup reportedly raised about $90 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in a round led by Robot Ventures, with Nvidia among the backers, as it debuted Hermes for Businesses.

items.headline: Anthropic offers startups a free year of its Claude Team plan and $1,000 in credits
items.summary: The AI firm said eligible early-stage startups can claim a year of its enterprise service plus token credits, a move to win over developers as rivals court the same customers.

items.headline: Vesta raises $30 million to bring AI 'agent swarms' to mortgage lenders
items.summary: TechCrunch reported the funding for Vesta, which is building teams of coordinated AI agents to automate steps in home-loan processing for lenders.

items.headline: Chip stocks slide as OpenAI's revenue reportedly trails the figure cited last month
items.summary: CNBC reported OpenAI told investors it reached about $50 billion in annualized revenue at end-September, below a $68 billion figure cited in September. Nvidia fell about 3%, Oracle about 6% and CoreWeave about 8%.

items.headline: Wall Street falls as a gauge of chipmakers drops 3.4%
items.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell about 1.4% on the AI-revenue jitters, Bloomberg reported, dragged by the sell-off in chip names; Treasuries rose and oil swung during the session.

items.headline: Treasuries gain on a strong 30-year auction even with yields near multi-decade highs
items.summary: US government bonds rallied after solid demand at a sale of 30-year debt, Bloomberg reported, a measure of relief after yields climbed to levels last seen years ago.

items.headline: Oil whipsaws as Trump rules out an Iran strike before the US midterms
items.summary: Crude jumped on renewed Middle East supply fears before settling below the day's highs after the president said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections, Bloomberg reported.

items.headline: F1's 2026 cars hit Marina Bay as Singapore's first sprint weekend gets under way
items.summary: The night race opens with practice and sprint qualifying on Friday, the first time Singapore hosts an F1 Sprint and the final sprint of the 2026 season, with the Grand Prix on Sunday.

items.headline: Shanghai Masters opens without Sinner as Fery stuns Cilic and Berrettini advances
items.summary: On the opening day of the Masters 1000, Britain's Arthur Fery beat Marin Cilic 7-6(2), 6-1 and Matteo Berrettini won; top seeds Zverev and Djokovic received first-round byes. Jannik Sinner withdrew before the event.

items.headline: South Africa and Australia begin their first Test at Kingsmead in Durban
items.summary: The three-match series opens on 9 October at Kingsmead, with Temba Bavuma's South Africa facing Australia after taking the preceding one-day series.

items.headline: Webb pinpoints the most distant fast radio burst ever detected
items.summary: Astronomers used the James Webb Space Telescope to locate the host galaxy of FRB 20240304B at a redshift of about 2.148 - roughly 3 billion years after the Big Bang - more than doubling the previous distance record, in a study published in Science.

items.headline: NASA unveils a more precise way to track Earth's wandering centre of mass
items.summary: NASA scientists describe a sharper method to measure how the planet's centre of mass shifts by a few millimetres through the year as water, ice and air migrate with the seasons.

fun_fact.headline: Scorpions glow under ultraviolet light
fun_fact.body: Scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light because compounds in their exoskeleton, including beta-carboline, fluoresce; field researchers hunt them at night with UV torches, and a freshly moulted scorpion does not glow until its new cuticle hardens.

puzzle.title: Through the Looking Glass
puzzle.body: You glance at a wall clock in a mirror. In the reflection, the hands clearly read 3:30. What is the actual time?
puzzle.approach: Picture the clock face flipped left-to-right, and work out which real time maps to the reflection.
puzzle.answer: 8:30. A left-right mirror makes the real time and its reflection add to 12:00 (reflection = 11:60 - real time), so 11:60 - 3:30 = 8:30.

word_puzzle.title: Common Threads
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four groups of four by a hidden link: FIRE, NET, CRIMSON, FOOT, DRAGON, FRAME, SNOW, RUBY, BUTTER, EYE, GUESS, SCARLET, HORSE, BASE, HOME, CHERRY.
word_puzzle.approach: Find the four words that each pair with the same hidden word; watch for FIRE, FOOT and NET as traps.
word_puzzle.answer: ___ FLY: BUTTER, DRAGON, HORSE, FIRE. ___ BALL: BASE, FOOT, EYE, SNOW. ___ WORK: NET, HOME, FRAME, GUESS. Shades of RED: CRIMSON, SCARLET, CHERRY, RUBY.
